Regards

Chris

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

plotting vegan's ordination with ggplot is fairly easy and gives you
full control of group-wise colorisation in your ordination. You just
need to extract the ordination coordinates from vegan's output and put
it into a dataframe.

The first is done by vegan's scores()-function, the second e.g. by
broom's tidy()

library(broom)
library(vegan)
library(ggplot2)

nmds <- metaMDS(yourdata, distance="bray", k=2)
sites <- tidy(scores(nmds), display="sites")
species <- tidy(scores(nmds, display="species"))

For the two dataframes you can add further factors as you whish, e.g.
sites$location or species$taxon. Now, its very easy to use ggplot2:

sites$treatment <- as.factor(....)

names(sites) <- c("Sample", "X", "Y", "Treatment")

ggplot()+
   geom_point(data=sites, aes(X, Y, col=Treatment), alpha=0) +
   geom_text(data=sites, aes(X, Y, label=Sample, col=Treatment)) +
   theme_bw() +
   coord_fixed()

Here is a tutorial without broom, which also gives a function to draw
hulls around your treatment levels:

https://chrischizinski.github.io/rstats/vegan-ggplot2/

and there must be walkthroughs how to add arrows, too.

Cheers,

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

> this was unanswered at SO, but i really would like to solve it.
>
> https://stackoverflow.com/questions/50234274/change-the-order-how-ggplot-draws-border-colors-in-geom-bar

For geom_point, I'd just suggest reordering the data.frame so
that the bits you wanted to be plotted last (Taxon B) are drawn
last. But that doesn't seem to apply to geom_bar: it is dependent on
factor level order which would mean that Taxon levels in the factor
would need to be c("A","C","B") which might not be desirable and
I believe would put B at the top all the time.

So this idea is a bit of a kludge, drawing the bar twice but with only
the red outline second time around.

> df <- data.frame(Taxon=c("A", "B", "C"),
>                       Counts=c(0.1,0.5,0.4),
>                       Treatment=rep("X1",3),
>                       Effect=factor(c("A","B","A")))
>      df$Effect <- factor(df$Effect, levels=c("A","B"), ordered=T)

You shouldn't really use df as a data.frame name since there is
a function df (the density function for the F distribution).

You don't need Effect for my solution (I couldn't get variations
on your code to work) - you can handle it in the scale_fill_manual.

So:

DF <- data.frame(Taxon = c("A", "B", "C"),

                  Counts = c(0.1,0.5,0.4),
                  Treatment = rep("X1",3),

                  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

ggplot(DF,aes(x = Treatment, y = Counts)) +
geom_bar(aes(fill=Taxon), stat='identity',
          position="fill", width=0.5,colour="black") +

scale_fill_manual("",values=c("gold", "green","yellow")) +

geom_bar(aes(colour=Taxon), stat='identity',
          position="fill", width=0.5, fill=NA) +
scale_color_manual("",values=c("transparent","red","transparent"))

How's that?

Regards,
Ron.
